hero.name: Saqib Ali
hero.lede: I lead antenna tracking system development at Orbitalink and research control for five-phase motor drives. Electrical Engineering at Aligarh Muslim University.

about.heading: Where control, power and RF meet
paragraphs: I'm an Electrical Engineering student at **Zakir Husain College of Engineering and Technology, AMU**, working where control systems, power electronics and RF meet.

At **Orbitalink** I lead antenna tracking systems end to end: a 435 MHz cross-Yagi antenna, a Fusion 360 chassis, motion firmware for hybrid servo drives, and adaptive control for a high-inertia mount.
At **IIT Ropar** I modelled a five-phase IPMSM, designed field-oriented control with loss-aware MTPA, and generated ePWM on a TI DSP to test the gate driver.

experience.intro: Research, industry and a university satellite programme.

items.org: Indian Institute of Technology Ropar · Rupnagar
bullets: Modelled a five-phase IPMSM in MATLAB/Simulink and designed dual-plane FOC with MTPA and flux weakening.
Derived loss-aware MTPA with Lagrange multipliers and a Newton–Raphson solver; implemented DTC and five-phase SVPWM.
Generated ePWM on a TI C2000 DSP in Code Composer Studio and tested the gate driver circuit.
Lead end-to-end development of a two-axis satellite antenna tracker, from chassis and RF to firmware.
Designed a 435 MHz cross-Yagi in MMANA-GAL with a phasing harness for circular polarisation.
Wrote firmware for NEMA23 hybrid servos on HSD57 drivers; porting it to STM32F411.

items.org: Orbitalink, with AMU Innovation Foundation · Aligarh
bullets: Designed an adaptive PID controller to stabilise and precisely point a high-inertia antenna tracker.
Built the tracker chassis model and two-axis PID positioning logic; support satellite tracking and equipment calibration.
